'''Karl M. Kadish''' (born 1945) is an American [[chemist]]. He is currently Hugh Roy and Lillie Cranz Cullen University Professor at the [[University of Houston]].<ref>{{Cite web
| url         = http://www.uh.edu/nsm/about/chairs-professorships/
| title       = Named Chairs & Professorships
| website     = uh.edu
| access-date = August 28, 2018
}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dr. Kadish received his B.S. from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1967 and his PhD from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1970.  After completing a postdoctoral fellowship at [[Louisiana State University]], [[New Orleans]] (LSUNO), he spent one year as [[Academic ranks in France|Chargé de Research]] at the University of Paris VI in France. He was an assistant professor at [[California State University, Fullerton]] from 1972 to 1976 and has been at the University of Houston since 1976, where he holds the position of Hugh Roy and Lillie Cranz Cullen University Professor in the Department of Chemistry.  Dr. Kadish has also held visiting professorships at [[Osaka University]] (Japan), the University of Sydney (Australia), the California Institute of Technology, the University of Rome, the University of Dijon, (France), Ecole Superieure de Chimie Industrielle de Lyon (ESCIL)(France) and Université Louis Pasteur (Strasbourg, France)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web
| url         = http://kadish.chem.uh.edu/vitae.html
| title       = Karl M. Kadish
| website     = kadish.chem.uh.edu
| access-date = August 28, 2018
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web
| url         = https://www.france-science.org/The-French-and-the-American.html
| title         = The French and the American Chemical Societies Honor the Career of a Professor from the University of Houston – Office for Science & Technology of the Embassy of France in the United States
| website         = france-science.org
| access-date         = August 28, 2018
| archive-date         = August 31, 2018
| archive-url         = https://web.archive.org/web/20180831035347/https://www.france-science.org/The-French-and-the-American.html
| url-status         = dead
}}</ref>

He has published over [http://kadish.chem.uh.edu/publications.html 600 research papers], the majority of which are on topics related to porphyrins, phthalocyanines, corroles and related macrocycles, while also editing more than 95 books on these topics and directing a research group, which, in total, has numbered over 125 different graduate students and postdoctoral associates.<ref name=":0" /> He is the founder and first president of the Fullerenes Division of [[Electrochemical Society|the Electrochemical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web
| url      = https://www.electrochem.org/dl/interface/sum/sum02/IF6-02-Pages18-19.pdf
| title    = Electrochemistry Society Fullerenes Division
| last     = Kadish
| year     = 2002
}}</ref> and since 1994 has organized or co-organized more than 25 symposia on the topic of fullerenes and carbon nanomaterials. He was a co-organizer of the first (2000), third (2004), sixth (2010), ninth (2016) and eleventh (2020) [http://www.icpp-spp.org/index.php International Conference on Porphyrins and Phthalocyanines]. Dr. Kadish is editor-in-chief of the ''[[Journal of Porphyrins and Phthalocyanines]]''<ref>{{Cite web
| url         = https://www.worldscientific.com/page/jpp/editorial-board
| title       = JPP Editorial Board
| website     = worldscientific.com
| access-date = August 28, 2018
}}</ref> and also serves as president of the Society of Porphyrins and Phthalocyanines (SPP), a position he has held continuously since June 2000.<ref>{{Cite web
| url         = https://www.spp-jpp.org/committee/
| title       = Society of Porphyrins & Phthalocyanines
| website     = icpp-spp.org
| access-date = August 28, 2018
}}</ref>

*Editor-in-chief, ''Journal of Porphyrins and Phthalocyanines'', 2001–present
*Chairman of Fullerenes Group of the Electrochemical Society, 1996–2000
*President, Society of Porphyrins and Phthalocyanines (SPP), 2000–present
